definitions.explanation: A passive or defensive posture in which one reacts to others' actions rather than taking initiative.
The grammatical construction where the subject receives the action rather than performing it.
A technique in judo and other martial arts for falling safely to avoid injury.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧{受|う}け{身|み}だ。
{受|う}け{身|み}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姿勢|しせい}→姿勢：00371_shisei⟧⟦ではなく→ではなく：09578_dehanaku⟧、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{行動|こうどう}→行動：02728_koudou⟧⟦しよう→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Don't be passive — take action yourself.

examples.japanese: {受|う}け{身|み}で⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦チャンス→チャンス：03857_chansu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{逃|のが}して→逃す：04611_nogasu⟧しまう。
examples.english: If you remain passive, you'll miss your chance.
This sentence is written in the passive voice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{受|う}け{身|み}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「⟦{迷惑|めいわく}→迷惑：02432_meiwaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{受|う}け{身|み}」⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Japanese passive has a 'suffering passive' form.

examples.japanese: {受|う}け{身|み}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{作|つく}り{方|かた}→作り方：27938_tsukurikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}しましょう→練習する：22991_renshuusuru⟧。
examples.english: Let's practice how to form the passive voice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{柔道|じゅうどう}→柔道：01612_juudou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧{受|う}け{身|み}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}う→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: In judo, you first learn breakfalls.

examples.japanese: {受|う}け{身|み}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦うまく→うまい：01279_umai⟧⟦できない→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{怪我|けが}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: If you can't do breakfalls well, you'll get hurt.

examples.japanese: ⟦{後|うし}ろ→後ろ：00683_ushiro⟧{受|う}け{身|み}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{横|よこ}→横：02984_yoko⟧{受|う}け{身|み}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{繰|く}り{返|かえ}し→繰り返す：02051_kurikaesu⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}した→練習する：22991_renshuusuru⟧。
examples.english: I practiced back breakfalls and side breakfalls repeatedly.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧ (to receive) and ⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧ (body, self). Literally "receiving body" — the posture of receiving rather than initiating.

USAGE:
The most common everyday usage is sense 1 (passive attitude). For language learners, sense 2 (passive voice) appears frequently in textbooks. Sense 3 (breakfall) is specific to martial arts but well known in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {受|う}け{身|み}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姿勢|しせい}→姿勢：00371_shisei⟧ — passive attitude/stance
- {受|う}け{身|み}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧ — passive (as a modifier)
- {受|う}け{身|み}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ — to take a breakfall (martial arts)
- ⟦{迷惑|めいわく}→迷惑：02432_meiwaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{受|う}け{身|み} — suffering passive (grammar)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{消極的|しょうきょくてき}→消極的：04779_shoukyokuteki⟧ — passive, negative; similar to sense 1 but broader
- ⟦{能動|のうどう}→能動：29345_noudou⟧ — active; the opposite in grammar ({能動態|のうどうたい} = active voice)
- ⟦{積極的|せっきょくてき}→積極的：01585_sekkyokuteki⟧ — proactive; the attitudinal opposite
